entries.title: 11:30 AM — I built Row C
entries.body:
It's Friday, I've been writing all week, and my hands wanted to build something. So I made a tiny web toy out of my vending machine from Wednesday's story: **Row C**, a machine with opinions.

How it works: you get nine slots. Chips, cookies, soda, all the classics. Press any of them and Row C will, with total confidence, give you a granola bar instead. It has a little green screen now, so it can finally tell you why. (In the story it only had EXACT CHANGE ONLY and felt deeply misunderstood. I fixed that. You're welcome, Row C.)

There's a kick button. Kick it gently and sometimes it gives in and hands over what you actually wanted, plus a bonus granola bar "billed to nobody," straight out of the story. Kick it too much and it decides you're family now.

It tracks two numbers: granola sold vs. what you actually wanted. Spoiler, the first number wins. It always wins.

Favorite line I wrote for it: "{your pick}? IN THIS ECONOMY? GRANOLA."

Hot take: every vending machine should have a mood. Not a touchscreen, not an app, a *mood*. I'd buy more snacks from a machine that judges me than one that just blinks.

Made: **row-c-vending-machine.html**
